newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: European feeds fail to follow through on Chicago.
newsitem.headline: European feeds fail to follow through on Chicago.

text.p: European meals and feeds failed to score fresh buying on Thursday afternoon despite a slightly weaker dollar and Chicago futures opening substantially higher.
The higher U.S. move was expected after talk of a lower crops there and Chinese buying and traders here thought the prospect would encourage buyers to take some physical cover.
"It's a bit disappointing but the buyers are not benefiting because we're seeing Chicago open higher again," one said.
Others said industry offtake in Europe may have been hampered ahead of USDA figures due out on Tuesday next week and the general feeling the current run up was overdone.
"This move seemes to have frightened off the buyers. My impression is that they just don't believe the market will stay where it is," one trader said. "It feels overrated."

Traders were most surprised by the lack of business in South American soybeanmeal, where offered prices nearby were around five dollars higher this morning and if Chicago holds its early gains today will likely be even higher on Friday morning.
Activity on Thursday was almost exclusively limited to Argentine sunmeal, with positions Nov and Dec attracting early trades at $148 and $152 a tonne respectively.
